The Democrats’ midterm “blue wave” wins gave them strong majorities in both chambers of Congress, new governors’ mansions and power in some unexpected places.
Voters dealt a stunning rebuke to Donald Trump – and his ruthless deportation campaign and violent ICE raids across the country were among the key issues that cost Republicans support.
But what will Democrats do about the immigration crackdown?
The final Senate race of this year’s midterm elections could be resolved tomorrow if Alaska election officials run the state’s ranked choice voting system to determine the result.
With 98% of ballots counted, Democratic challenger Mary Peltola is out in front with 49.98% of the vote. By contrast, incumbent Republican senator Dan S Sullivan has a 45.93% share, according to the latest Associated Press figures.
In terms of actual voting numbers, Peltola is ahead by just over 11,000, with 141,637 compared to Sullivan’s 130,162. All eyes will be on Peltola to see if she can keep the pace to achieve 50% of the ballot, two weeks on from the election.
If not, then voters’ second choice votes will be counted. The outcome will determine the final balance of power in the chamber for the next two years, with Democrats already holding a 55-44 majority.
It comes in a turbulent Alaska race, which has seen president Trump demand that Peltola be removed from the ballot and prosecuted. Piling on, Alaska’s Republican governor has since ordered an investigation into Peltola’s campaign.
A New York Times investigation reported that operatives working with Peltola’s campaign helped recruit another Dan Sullivan – Dan J Sullivan – a retired teacher from Petersburg, to split the incumbent’s vote. Peltola and her campaign have denied this.
The ‘other’ Sullivan, who stood as an independent candidate, has only received 4,684 votes – a 1.65% share – and is looking unlikely to be the cause of the Republican senator’s failure should he not retain his seat.
Elsewhere, president Trump has arrived in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit, where he is due to meet south east Asian leaders and take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.

In other developments:
Donald Trump defended his commerce secretary Howard Lutnick after he came under fire for allegedly slow-walking export restrictions on Nvidia chips to China. This comes after treasury secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC last week that he has been pushing “for months” to add Megaspeed, the data center company led by an alleged Chinese spy who was reportedly in a relationship with ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, to the US trade blacklist.
Trump blasted the new leadership of CBS News’ 60 Minutes, which was overhauled under the network’s conservative editor-in-chief Bari Weiss. In a social media post, the president was particularly critical of a report on the more than 800 American service members wounded and 23 killed in the war in Iran that 60 Minutes aired on Sunday.
Trump also said that he would “not mind” seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as the chief executive officer of Nvidia. The president says the ex-CEO has learned a lesson, and denied that national security has been put at risk.
The president also continued to shift responsibility to the Biden administration for the nationwide ground stop over the weekend. Trump said that he needed more funding to overhaul the outdated telecommunication system responsible for the disruptions.
The Trump administration has warned Elizabeth Warren, the senior Democratic senator expected to chair the powerful Senate banking committee, that she could face “significant legal consequences” if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into Donald Trump. The warning mirrors other letters justice department officials have sent to Democratic lawmakers who have indicated they will investigate the Trump administration when the party becomes the majority in Congress next year.
A federal appeals court heard arguments in Donald Trump’s hush money case, as the president tries to see the case shifted to federal court where he could have it dismissed on grounds of immunity. The hearing concerned a May 2024 ruling that found Trump guilty on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film star Stormy Daniels.

המרוץ האחרון לסנאט במסגרת בחירות האמצע בארצות הברית עשוי להסתיים בהכרעה עבור המועמדת הדמוקרטית מרי פלטולה, המובילה באלסקה עם אחוז קולות גבוה לקראת סיום הספירה. במידה ואף מועמד לא יגיע לרוב מוחלט, תופעל שיטת הבחירה המדורגת של המדינה כדי לקבוע את תוצאת הבחירות הסופית שתקבע את מאזן הכוחות בקונגרס.

במקביל, נשיא ארה"ב דונלד טראמפ הגיע למנילה שבפיליפינים להשתתפות בפסגת איגוד אומות דרום-מזרח אסיה (ASEAN), שם הוא מקיים פגישות עם מנהיגי האזור. בזירה הפוליטית המקומית, טראמפ הגן על שר המסחר האמריקאי הוורד לוטניק מפני ביקורת ציבורית, והתייחס גם לסוגיות נוספות הנוגעות למדיניות חוץ, למערך התקשורת הפדרלי ולתיקים המשפטיים המתנהלים נגדו.
